verdicts.reason: A keeps the original centred column: logo top-centre, then can, headline, CTA and legal. But the CTA pill is small and weak, there is a big dead gap between the headline and the CTA, and the oversized sticker placeholder crowds the headline. B has a stronger full-width CTA, but it shrinks the SOLSTICE logo into a tiny top-right corner mark off the centre axis, which weakens the brand, and it has the same sticker crowding.

A moves the headline above the product, changing the original order. The sticker is jammed right under the headline, there is a large empty band between the can and the small CTA, and the composition looks top-heavy. B keeps the original order (product, headline, CTA) and has a strong CTA, but the logo is pushed to a tiny off-axis top-right corner and the sticker placeholder sits awkwardly between the can and the headline.

A keeps the original order and has a prominent CTA, but the logo is shrunk into an off-axis top-right corner and the sticker crowds the headline. B pushes the headline against the top edge with no logo above it, moves the brand mark to a tiny spot below the CTA (it barely reads as a brand), stacks the sticker right under the headline, and leaves dead space between the can and the CTA.
